detail: Acceptance criterion 'the matching row is removed from the bugs table in testing/flows/' is excluded under Out of scope although the story has no Test scope section permitting that. Add a case (e.g. file/content check on testing/flows/catalog.md) verifying the bug row is gone.
location: Story Acceptance Criteria; _index.md Out of scope

detail: No case shows an admin can still call the v1 update (UpdateItemV1 also got RequireAuthorization); add a happy-path admin PUT api-version=1.0 expecting success and persisted change.
Largely repeats TC-01 to TC-04; the only addition is the combined unchanged-state snapshot. Could fold into those cases.
The non-admin 403 case does not cover the v1 update route (PUT /items?api-version=1.0), which is separately registered.

AC requires the fixme marker removed from ordering-api.spec.ts, that test passing, and the rest of the file passing. The plan declares this out of scope and has no case running that command; add a case that runs the spec command and asserts all tests pass with no fixme.

AC requires the matching row removed from the bugs table in testing/flows/. No case verifies this, and the story has no Test scope excluding it; add a verification case or have the story author mark it out of scope.
The story states 404 only for another buyer's order, not for a nonexistent id; the cited 'Technical Notes' source does not say this. Drop the claim or raise it as an open question.
The story does not state the anonymous-request status. 401 is implied by 'signed-in' but not stated; list it as an open question or justify it from the story.

The case asserts specific pass and fixme counts (14/5 becoming 15/4). The story only says the spec counts were updated. The expectation should be that the counts in testing/flows/ordering.md are consistent with the spec after the fixme is removed, not hard-coded numbers.

Asserts exact spec counts (14 pass/5 fixme becomes 15 pass/4 fixme) and a flow-row marker, but AC 3 only requires removing the matching row from the bugs table. The numbers are fragile and unverified against the repo; state the expectation as one fewer fixme and one more pass than the baseline, or drop it.

The case expects the body to contain 'the two items'. The test only asserts the sorted unitPrice values [69.99, 179.99], not item names or descriptions. The prices still identify the items in this scenario, so the gap is minor.
Asserts a 401 for a missing token, which the story never states (it only implies a token is used). Keep it only if framed as a regression guard, or move to Open questions.
TC-02, 03 and 04 say 'a valid CreateOrderRequest' without specifying items/fields; TC-01 pins productId 2 quantity 2. Specify the same body in all cases so two engineers write the same test.
Hard-codes '15 pass, 4 fixme' counts taken from Implementation Notes rather than the AC; brittle and beyond the AC, which only requires the bug row removal. Assert the row/fixme marker absence only.

The case says step 2 returns exactly 6 orders. The test asserts the count equals the count recorded just before the POST, which is 7 after the earlier serial tests. It is weaker than a literal value but correct for the shared state, so the case text is arguably stale.
